_comment: Generic Pi-hole v6 profile used by scripts/pihole_tool.rb. value=null means network-specific: set it in config/settings.local.json. apply=false means advisory (audit reports it, apply never changes it).

dns.upstreams.why: One provider pair gives consistent answers and one privacy policy. Default here: Quad9 (validates DNSSEC, blocks known-malicious domains). Alternatives: Cloudflare 1.1.1.1/1.0.0.1, or 127.0.0.1#5335 for a local unbound. pihole_bench.rb shows which is fastest for you.
dns.upstreams.ui: Settings → DNS → Upstream DNS Servers / Custom DNS servers

dns.listeningMode.why: Answers only devices on directly connected subnets, so an accidental port forward can't create an open resolver. Use ALL only for clients that reach the Pi through a router (other VLAN, VPN subnet not terminated on the Pi).

dns.blockTTL.why: Clients cache blocked answers this many seconds; large values make new allowlist entries look broken.

dns.replyWhenBusy.why: During the brief gravity database swap, answer normally instead of leaving clients waiting on dropped queries.

dns.domainNeeded.why: Never forward single-label names (e.g. 'printer') to the internet.

dns.bogusPriv.why: Never forward reverse lookups of private IP ranges to the internet.

dns.blocking.mode.why: Blocked names get 0.0.0.0/:: and clients give up instantly. Pi-hole's recommended mode.

dns.cache.size.why: The default fits home networks; above 10k lookups slow down. Raise only if the audit reports live cache evictions.

dns.cache.optimizer.why: Serve just-expired records instantly while refreshing them in the background.

dns.specialDomains.iCloudPrivateRelay.why: Stops Apple devices from tunnelling DNS past Pi-hole via iCloud Private Relay.

dns.specialDomains.mozillaCanary.why: Tells Firefox not to auto-enable DNS-over-HTTPS, which would bypass Pi-hole.

dns.specialDomains.designatedResolver.why: Blocks DDR discovery (_dns.resolver.arpa) so clients don't upgrade to an encrypted resolver that bypasses Pi-hole.

dns.dnssec.why: Validating upstreams (Quad9, Cloudflare, Google) already reject bad signatures; enable only if yours doesn't. The audit tests this.

dns.revServers.why: Conditional forwarding so clients show by name: ["true,<LAN CIDR>,<router IP>[,<local domain>]"].

webserver.acl.why: Limit the web UI/API to LAN (+VPN): "+127.0.0.1,+[::1],+<LAN CIDR>". Last match wins; everything else is denied.

webserver.port.why: Pi-hole's default: plain HTTP without a forced HTTPS redirect (no certificate warnings) for a web UI that is only reachable inside the LAN. HTTPS stays available on 443 if you want it.

ntp.ipv4.active.why: Pi-hole runs an NTP server on UDP/123. Turn it off if no device uses the Pi as its time server (keep ntp.sync on).
